21-01-opti-1: In 1786, Benjamin Franklin printed a map of a river inside the ocean.
21-01-opti-2: Today, waves roll onto a Florida beach. Something shiny washes in.
21-01-opti-3: It's as wide as a cookie, and shaped like a heart.
21-01-opti-4: A seed? From across the ocean?
21-01-opti-5: It grew in a giant pod on a rainforest vine, far to the south.
21-01-opti-6: It fell into a river, then rode the ocean currents for months.
21-01-opti-7: Some sea hearts even sail to the beaches of Scotland.
21-01-opti-8: How can one plant start new plants so far away?
21-01-welcome: Our film starts on a Florida beach, with a seed from far away. First, look closely at a dandelion.
21-01-lesson: Today you're the seed scientist. Watch a blossom become an apple, test seeds, then look inside a lily.
21-01-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
21-01-assign: Time to show what you know. Read each case, then tell how each plant makes new plants.
how-21-01-compare: Put the fan by one tray and the tub of water by the other: drag them, or tap each one, then tap a tray. Press Test it. Then swap them and press it again.
how-21-01-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap a clue you see, then pick what it is. Predict how it traveled, and watch its home appear.
how-21-01-write: Pick one of the four cases from Part A. Explain how that plant reproduces and what would happen if something went wrong. Use at least one of the science words under the boxes.
how-21-01-partc: Draw a nature scene that shows two different ways plants make new plants. Add arrows to show what moves.
